title: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2026-03-07

Opens [Matt 13](/bible/matthew/13) · [Dan 4](/bible/daniel/4) · [Matt 24](/bible/matthew/24) · [1 Thess 5](/bible/1-thessalonians/5) · [Gen 2](/bible/genesis/2) · [Gen 11](/bible/genesis/11) · [Gen 24](/bible/genesis/24) · [Gen 29](/bible/genesis/29) · [Gen 34](/bible/genesis/34) · [Judg 14](/bible/judges/14) · [2 Sam 11](/bible/2-samuel/11) · [Tobit 8](/bible/tobit/8) · [2 Sam 13](/bible/2-samuel/13) · [Deut 24](/bible/deuteronomy/24) · [Exod 21](/bible/exodus/21) · [Prov 20](/bible/proverbs/20) · and 2 more below
## Introduction *[[13:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=813s)]* Marriage beyond romance, from Eden to modern confusion. Deacon Yashua opens with a hot take on Iran and the signs: prophecy should move Israel to correction, not entertain it, and if the days are being shortened then marriage and household order cannot be treated casually. He then lays out how God instituted marriage as a covenant of order and responsibility, how the forefathers' marriages were built on mission rather than attraction, and how every romance-driven story in scripture documents its cost. Romance itself is a Roman word, and kneeling, rings, the white dress, the wedding industry, and the honeymoon are cultural additions. The class closes with the husband's provision, leadership, and integrity, and the wife's unconditional submission and reverence. ## In The News - *[[19:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=1162s)]* **Donald Trump saying his own morality and his own mind are the only things that can stop him, and he does not need international law.** — Out of the beast's own mouth: no limits from Congress, no international law. Daniel 4:17 said the Most High sets up over the kingdom of men the basest of men. - *[[46:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=2811s)]* **The Wikipedia entry on romance, read on screen.** — Romance is passionate attraction, prioritizing feelings and intimacy over practical concerns, a relationship that may be premarital or absent a commitment, and an idealization that overrides all other considerations. Individualistic choice in marriage and sexual partners came from it. The word derives from the Latin Romanus, meaning Rome, and in the Middle Ages meant narrative verse about chivalry and love. - *[[58:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=3527s)]* **The entry on chivalry, with its picture of a kneeling knight.** — An informal code of conduct that developed in France between 1170 and 1220, tied to Christian knighthood. Keep that picture in mind for the origin of kneeling to propose. - *[[1:37:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=5862s)]* **A definition of aged together, put up by the tech team.** — The long-term intertwined journey of partners growing old side by side, shared history, mutual support through life's changes, accepting the natural aging process, and navigating challenges as a team. Aged means refined, like wine and cheese. Everything else gets established first or the romance is fleeting. - *[[1:41:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=6107s)]* **The definition of ravished: to fill with intense delight and rapture; delight, charm, enthrall, captivate, fascinate.** — There is your passion, after the foundation of the marriage is set correctly. You do not seek this first, like buying furniture and rugs before you know the walls of the house will hold. - *[[1:49:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=6544s)]* **The origin of kneeling to propose.** — It comes from medieval chivalry, feudalism, and religious tradition, where kneeling symbolized loyalty, submission, and respect to a higher authority. Knights knelt before lords and noble women, and it was adopted as a romantic gesture of servitude. No man should kneel to propose; the wife submits to the husband. The Bible shows men taking wives, not proposing on one knee. - *[[1:52:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=6751s)]* **The origin of engagement rings.** — A Roman custom: iron rings signified a binding contract between families and the transfer of the daughter to the man, a legal agreement, not romance. Romans believed a vein ran from the fourth finger to the heart. The first recorded diamond ring was Archduke Maximilian's in 1477, and the diamond only became universal after the De Beers campaign of 1947, A Diamond Is Forever, which added the two-months-salary expectation to sell diamonds through the Depression. - *[[1:57:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=7042s)]* **The origin of wedding rings.** — Egyptian, around 3000 BC, braided reeds and leather with the circle for eternity and the hole for a gateway to the unknown. Rome popularized metal rings, and the Catholic Church adopted the ring in the twelfth century, turning a pagan custom into a sacrament. The Bible never commands or describes wedding rings. - *[[2:06:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=7601s)]* **The origin of the honeymoon.** — Fifth-century European and Norse newlyweds drank mead, fermented honey, for one full moon cycle for fertility, a month spent drunk, with the implication that the intense first love would wane like the moon. The travel version began in nineteenth-century Britain as a bridal tour to relatives who missed the wedding. A mishmash of cultures. - *[[2:15:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=8101s)]* **A commentator on selecting a partner.** — You are choosing a whole lifestyle, not a person: their sleep schedule, money habits, stress, family drama, cleanliness, work ethic, and coping mechanisms. Love does not cancel flaws, it makes you tolerate them longer. Can you live with this person's version of Tuesday for the rest of your life? You do not fix somebody's lifestyle from the inside. - *[[2:17:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=8229s)]* **A commentator on when a man is safe to love.** — A man is safe when he can discipline his own emotions while still experiencing them, then understand other people's emotions and help them through. Otherwise he blows up his own feelings and attacks others for having theirs. Brothers who cannot handle correction blow up outwardly or go sensual and separate themselves; babies, not manly at all. - *[[2:28:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=8899s)]* **A woman teacher on a wife's conduct: soft, respectful, quiet, and learning to keep her mouth shut, citing 1 Peter 3:1.** — If you fear God you do what he says. Women hear one side and jump to the man's issues to deflect; it is not your job to fix his issues but to stay in your lane. Many wives have never submitted in everything once in their whole marriage. - *[[2:31:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=9104s)]* **The same teacher: if submission depends on his behavior, it is not submission, it is manipulation.** — God said submit in everything with no caveat. Submission is a spiritual assignment from God, not a transactional engagement. If that offends you, you are out of order. - *[[2:40:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=9614s)]* **The definition of reverence.** — A profound, heartfelt attitude of awe, respect, and holy fear toward God, manifesting as obedience, worship, and submission to his authority. Reverence for a husband is beyond respect and cannot be done as a job description; pray for that spirit if you do not have it. ## Scriptures Opened **[Matthew 13:16-17](/bible/matthew/13#v16)** *[[14:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=870s)]* > [16](/bible/matthew/13#v16) But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. > > [17](/bible/matthew/13#v17) For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them. - Blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear; many prophets and righteous men desired to see these things and did not. Our forefathers described a serpent with all its power in its head as best they could; they did not know what a missile was. We are blessed to see it and to have leaders with the spirit to explain it. - Prophecy should move us to correction. It is not entertainment. For a certain amount of people it is just something they like, and it never moves them to urgency or self-assessment. What does it profit if you see all the prophecy of the last six years and are still caught in the mess? **[Daniel 4:17](/bible/daniel/4#v17)** *[[18:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=1083s)]* > [17](/bible/daniel/4#v17) This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men. - The Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men. World events are never random; his hand is down here. When war rises and alliances shift, scripture already told us, and it said who would lead. **[Matthew 24:6-9](/bible/matthew/24#v6)** *[[20:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=1202s)]* > [6](/bible/matthew/24#v6) And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. > > [7](/bible/matthew/24#v7) For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. > > [8](/bible/matthew/24#v8) All these are the beginning of sorrows. > > [9](/bible/matthew/24#v9) Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake. - Ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars; see that ye be not troubled. We are not troubled because we do not sleep as others do; each event moves us ten yards down the field. It should only trouble you if you are not in the spirit to repent with urgency. - All these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. Nation against nation, famines, pestilences, earthquakes: the food shortages, COVID, and the brethren the Lord received are the beginning of sorrows. Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted and kill you; Jacob's trouble is not here yet, though it can escalate quickly on the Lord's timeline. Precepts: - **[2 Esdras 15:29-30](/bible/2-esdras/15#v29)** > [29](/bible/2-esdras/15#v29) Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble. > > [30](/bible/2-esdras/15#v30) Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians. The nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, carried as the wind, and the Carmanians, Iran, shall go forth as wild boars and join battle with them and waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians. That is unity and nukes, and neither is present yet. What you are seeing is contractions. - **[Matthew 24:22](/bible/matthew/24#v22)** > [22](/bible/matthew/24#v22) And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened. Except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved. Shortened means events accelerate, like a woman in travail: each contraction inches closer. The stage is being set, and the Lord can put spirit on men to move things along quicker. **[1 Thessalonians 5:1-2,11,14-22](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v1)** *[[24:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=1488s)]* > [1](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v1) But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. > > [2](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v2) For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. > > [11](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v11) Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do. > > [14](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v14) Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men. > > [15](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v15) See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men. > > [16](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v16) Rejoice evermore. > > [17](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v17) Pray without ceasing. > > [18](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v18) In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you. > > [19](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v19) Quench not the Spirit. > > [20](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v20) Despise not prophesyings. > > [21](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v21) Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. > > [22](/bible/1-thessalonians/5#v22) Abstain from all appearance of evil. - Of the times and seasons ye have no need that I write; the day of the Lord cometh as a thief in the night. Every global event our people asked, is this the time? Christ gave us signs but no dates, because much depends on when the 144,000 are sealed. The rest of the chapter is about not sleeping and being sober, and sobriety takes abstinence from sin. - Wherefore comfort yourselves together and edify one another. Warn them that are unruly, those who will not follow what the Bible says, as in the marriage topic; comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men, render not evil for evil. Rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing, in every thing give thanks: this is the will of God concerning you. - Quench not the Spirit, despise not prophesyings, prove all things, hold fast that which is good, abstain from all appearance of evil. The more signs we see, the more urgently we should repent and strengthen our households. You think you are ready for the affliction when you cannot even endure each other? If the days are getting shorter, marriage and family order cannot be treated casually anymore. **[Genesis 2:21-24](/bible/genesis/2#v21)** *[[36:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=2218s)]* > [21](/bible/genesis/2#v21) And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; > > [22](/bible/genesis/2#v22) And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. > > [23](/bible/genesis/2#v23) And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. > > [24](/bible/genesis/2#v24) Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh. - Marriage is the foundation of nation building. Outside of sanctifying the seventh day, the union of man and wife is the first institution God ordained, before governments or ceremonies, and the first thing Satan attacked. Marriages struggle because most of us enter with expectations formed by the world, not scripture; a false definition fails before any action does. If marriage is defined as emotional fulfillment, constant romance, or personal happiness, then sacrifice, authority, submission, correction, and endurance break it. A marriage enters its biblical phase when the trials come, as a fast begins when the hunger does. - The Lord took one of Adam's ribs, made a woman, and brought her unto the man. There was no feast and no courtship; God formed the woman and brought her. It begins with order and authority: the woman was taken out of man, not formed separately from the dust as the artwork and the apple story subtly teach. The breath of life was breathed into the man, because the authority and responsibility were his. - This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman. That is what the modern vows, in sickness and in health, are a rudiment of; the real vows are what Tobias prayed in Tobit 8. People writing their own vows go further and further from what God ordained. - Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother and cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh. One flesh means inseparable, but not up your wife's skirt all the time as her best friend: without God there is no wife and no family, so the man's priorities stay in God's order. Marriage began as a divine institution, and what we call marriage today is a human invention. Precepts: - **[Malachi 2:14](/bible/malachi/2#v14)** > [14](/bible/malachi/2#v14) Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. The Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, thy companion and the wife of thy covenant. God was in the first marriage and is in every marriage. A covenant is a contract of commitment and obligation, not feelings. You understand your phone plan and a sports contract but not this one. Treacherous or not, one flesh is still your companion. She will not be bad forever; hormones change, and you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, drive, and wake-up. **[Genesis 11:29-31](/bible/genesis/11#v29)** *[[1:01:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=3718s)]* > [29](/bible/genesis/11#v29) And Abram and Nahor took them wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah. > > [30](/bible/genesis/11#v30) But Sarai was barren; she had no child. > > [31](/bible/genesis/11#v31) And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter in law, his son Abram’s wife; and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan; and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there. - Abram and Nahor took them wives; Sarai was barren; and Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai and went forth from Ur toward Canaan. No attraction language, and what follows immediately is that they moved to another country and she did not buck. You marry a whole family: father-in-law, daughter-in-law, nephew, and all the risk and hardship shared. - Men traditionally date down the scale and marry whoever they are with who provides what they need; women get an inflated view of their rank from the attention and hold out for five-foot-ten with a tape measure. Attention does not always mean you are pretty, sister; it may mean he thought you were an easy mark. If your type is about appearance rather than character, examine where your head is. Partnership and intimacy come later as the marriage progresses. **[Genesis 24:67](/bible/genesis/24#v67)** *[[1:06:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=3989s)]* > [67](/bible/genesis/24#v67) And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death. - Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother's tent, she became his wife, and he loved her. She becomes his wife, then he loved her. Brothers three months into proving saying I love her usually have mommy issues. There is no love at first sight; what we call that is lust at first sight, and disorder follows when it is the primary mover. - Genesis 26:8: Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah his wife. Intimacy is not just sex; it is being the truest form of yourself before your spouse, laughing and having a good time, and it came after they were married, not before. Some of you want that now, knee to knee at the school feeling the electricity, hormones clouding everything so you rationalize what you were warned about. **[Genesis 29:9-11,17-20](/bible/genesis/29#v9)** *[[1:11:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=4278s)]* > [9](/bible/genesis/29#v9) And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep: for she kept them. > > [10](/bible/genesis/29#v10) And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother. > > [11](/bible/genesis/29#v11) And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept. > > [17](/bible/genesis/29#v17) Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured. > > [18](/bible/genesis/29#v18) And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter. > > [19](/bible/genesis/29#v19) And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me. > > [20](/bible/genesis/29#v20) And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her. - When Jacob saw Rachel he rolled the stone from the well's mouth and watered the flock, flexing like a bird puffing its chest, did she see me? Right away it altered his behavior. Abram and Isaac got married and went about God's business; Jacob lost his mind over Rachel. The kiss was a greeting, like the Northern Kingdom's kiss on the cheek, not making out. - Leah was tender eyed, but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured, and Jacob loved Rachel and served seven years that seemed but a few days for the love he had to her. Contrast Isaac: married, then loved. Jacob's love was based on physical beauty, emotional attraction, and romantic motivation, and what followed was deception, competition between Leah, Rachel, and the handmaids, and family tension. Scripture does not hide the cost of romance-driven decisions; it documents it. **[Genesis 34:1-3](/bible/genesis/34#v1)** *[[1:16:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=4599s)]* > [1](/bible/genesis/34#v1) And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land. > > [2](/bible/genesis/34#v2) And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her. > > [3](/bible/genesis/34#v3) And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel. - Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land, and Shechem saw her, took her, and defiled her. It sounds romantic, he was enamoured, but what it says is he saw, took, and defiled, because evil intent drives what is done by the eyes. - His soul clave unto Dinah and he loved the damsel: the love comes after the violation. Then came more deception, the slaughter of the men of Shechem, and turmoil under Jacob. Visual attraction produced violence and bloodshed, as it still does when one man is jealous of another. **[Judges 14:1-3](/bible/judges/14#v1)** *[[1:19:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=4746s)]* > [1](/bible/judges/14#v1) And Samson went down to Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines. > > [2](/bible/judges/14#v2) And he came up, and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines: now therefore get her for me to wife. > > [3](/bible/judges/14#v3) Then his father and his mother said unto him, Is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said unto his father, Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well. - Samson saw a woman of the Philistines in Timnath and told his parents, get her for me to wife. They asked, is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren? He answered, get her for me, for she pleaseth me well. Purely visual reasoning, like the brother who sees nothing he likes in his congregation and grabs one online or in another city, hoping she will understand all this later. - What came of it: conflict with the Philistines, betrayal, thirty men dead, escalation into war, and in Judges 16 the loss of his vow, his strength, his eyes, and his freedom. A physical cautionary tale that men who move that way give up their preeminence. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if it is the only thing you move on. **[2 Samuel 11:2](/bible/2-samuel/11#v2)** *[[1:23:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=4982s)]* > [2](/bible/2-samuel/11#v2) And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon. - David walked on the roof and saw a woman washing herself, and she was very beautiful to look upon. He saw, inquired, and took, the same pattern as Shechem. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house for the rest of his days, though the Lord forgave him. - Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage. She looks good, I have to marry her so I can have her. Precepts: - **[2 Samuel 14:25](/bible/2-samuel/14#v25)** > [25](/bible/2-samuel/14#v25) But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him. In all Israel there was none so much praised as Absalom for his beauty, without blemish from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. Beauty became his identity, and behind it came ambition, rebellion against his father, civil war, and death hanging by that very hair. Whenever physical attraction is in the forefront, the Bible shows trouble behind it. - **[Proverbs 6:25](/bible/proverbs/6#v25)** > [25](/bible/proverbs/6#v25) Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids. Lust not after her beauty in thine heart, neither let her take thee with her eyelids. She gives you the look back, the sparks fly, and you have lost your mind. - **[Proverbs 7:10](/bible/proverbs/7#v10)** > [10](/bible/proverbs/7#v10) And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart. A woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart. The physical again, meant to entice, and it works. Solomon knew how intoxicating it is; he said not one woman in a thousand. **[Tobit 8:4-8](/bible/tobit/8#v4)** *[[1:33:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=5612s)]* > [4](/bible/tobit/8#v4) And after that they were both shut in together, Tobias rose out of the bed, and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray that God would have pity on us. > > [5](/bible/tobit/8#v5) Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art thou, O God of our fathers, and blessed is thy holy and glorious name for ever; let the heavens bless thee, and all thy creatures. > > [6](/bible/tobit/8#v6) Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: thou hast said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make unto him an aid like unto himself. > > [7](/bible/tobit/8#v7) And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together. > > [8](/bible/tobit/8#v8) And she said with him, Amen. - The pattern so far: Adam and Eve, divine creation and order; Abraham and Sarah, covenant and mission; Isaac and Rebekah, ordained and then love; Jacob and Rachel, attraction and complication. The Bible rarely describes the beauty of wives; Rebekah is known for hospitality and faith, Zipporah's looks are never mentioned, and Elisabeth is called righteous. Sarah's beauty is mentioned only for external threats. Proverbs 31 never says her price is above rubies because she is a baddie. Social media validates sisters with likes and breeds a subtle vanity; be presentable, but do not put status on appearance. - Tobias rose out of the bed and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray. Grounded in that order, love becomes stronger, joy and passion follow, and the marriage becomes more durable over time. ## Class Questions - **What should prophecy do for the Israelite?** Move us to correction, not entertain us. Blessed are your eyes for they see, Matthew 13:16-17; abstain from all appearance of evil, 1 Thessalonians 5:22. The more signs we see, the more urgently we repent and strengthen our households. - **Why is the current war with Iran not the end?** The dragons of Arabia must first come out united, and then the Carmanians join battle with them, 2 Esdras 15:29-30. Neither Arab unity nor wasting the land is present yet; these are contractions, and the days being shortened, Matthew 24:22, means events accelerate. - **What was the first institution God ordained after the Sabbath?** The union of man and wife, Genesis 2:21-24. God formed the woman from the man and brought her to him with no courtship, no feast, and no attraction language. - **What is marriage according to Malachi 2:14?** A covenant with the Lord as witness, a contract of commitment and obligation, not feelings. - **What is the difference between Isaac and Jacob in how they came to love their wives?** Isaac took Rebekah, she became his wife, and then he loved her, Genesis 24:67. Jacob loved Rachel first for her beauty, Genesis 29:17-20, and deception, competition, and family tension followed. - **Name the romance-driven cautionary tales the class covered.** Shechem saw and took Dinah, Genesis 34:1-3; Samson demanded the Philistine woman who pleased him well, Judges 14:1-3; David saw Bathsheba, 2 Samuel 11:2; Absalom was praised for his beauty, 2 Samuel 14:25. Each produced violence, betrayal, adultery, or rebellion. - **Where does the word romance come from?** From the Latin Romanus, meaning Rome or Roman. It came to mean chivalric love poetry in the Middle Ages and is a Roman custom, not a biblical one. - **What did Tobias pray on his wedding night?** That God gave Adam Eve for an helper and stay, of them came mankind; I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly; mercifully ordain that we may become aged together, Tobit 8:4-8. Sarah answered Amen. - **What does a man and wife that agree together mean in Sirach 25:1?** She agrees to follow the scriptures for a wife without contingencies, and he agrees to follow them as a husband. Not shared taste in music or food. - **What color did the king's virgin daughters wear?** Garments of divers colours, 2 Samuel 13:18, and raiment of needlework and wrought gold, Psalms 45:13-14. The white dress is Queen Victoria's 1840 fashion, not a symbol of purity. - **What does the Bible give a newly married man instead of a honeymoon?** One year free at home, not going to war or charged with business, to cheer up his wife, Deuteronomy 24:5. A year to establish the household, not a vacation. - **What are the husband's responsibilities?** Provision, leadership, instruction, and honour: her food, raiment, and duty of marriage not diminished, Exodus 21:10; provide for his own house, 1 Timothy 5:8; sacrificial headship, Ephesians 5:23-25; dwell with her according to knowledge, 1 Peter 3:7; walk in integrity, Proverbs 20:7. - **What makes a wife beautiful according to Sirach 26?** The ordering of her house, a shamefaced and faithful woman with a continent mind, fair feet with a constant heart, Sirach 26:15-18. Order equals beauty. - **When is submission not submission?** When it depends on the husband's behavior; then it is manipulation. Wives submit in every thing as unto the Lord, Ephesians 5:22-24, and reverence their husbands, Ephesians 5:33. - **What is the order in 1 Corinthians 11:3?** The head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. ## In Closing *[[2:44:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEm9Tb1jLDg&t=9868s)]* Keep the ordinances as they were delivered: the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. When marriage is grounded in that order, love becomes stronger, you have the passion and the joy, not romance but the more meaningful feelings behind it, and the marriage becomes more durable over time. There is a lot going on in the earth, and it behooves us not just to be aware of it but to take urgent action. Prophecy is not entertainment, brothers and sisters; it is a sign for us to correct ourselves and get things in order, individually and as a people. ## Announcements & References - Shout out to Captain Zeff and Captain IBL; a variation of this class was given at February's new moon and is on the IUIC Phoenix YouTube page. - The pride and submission piece will be taken deeper on the show, the power hour. - Bishop Nathanyel's class is up next. - Like and subscribe to IUIC Phoenix; the channel passed 32,000 subscribers and is aiming for 35,000.
